Good morning.
As economists and markets ponder what’s ahead for next week and beyond, a big question looms:
How will the US Treasury react to fluctuations in longer-term bond yields? Specifically, what will the balance be between:
  Further market intervention: Bigger and broader intervention tools;
  Fiscal adjustment: Outlining genuine fiscal reform plans;
  Passive tolerance: Accepting high and rising rates; and
  Risk mitigation: Focusing policies on softening the blow to the most interest-sensitive segments of the economy and society.
More to follow.
(The 30-year yield chart below is from Bloomberg.)
#economy #markets #yields #bonds

In the west US/UK/AUS/CAN a circa top 1% entry income is circa 2-500k USD pending which country

After tax they can barely afford a mortgage on a 1-2m USD property

When people think of 1% income earners they imagine 20m mansion owners - this isnt even 0.1% its 0.01%. Thats the 1% of the 1%

When incomes alone no longer allow you at any level to have wealth you are living in a Feudalist society

For most of the world this has always been standard- people who travel know that western idea of middle class doesnt exist in most places

Part of globalisation is deepening of world markets - as the wealth is spread across the world you also redistribute that middle class wealth elsewhere

So globally standard of living on average is higher in an absolute sense but it means the west also reverts back to the norm

If you are familiar with other countries its jarring when people in west complain about not having enough to buy a house or get holidays - for most the world they already live that as the standard

The "middle class" is already an outdated term - there is no real middle class the way it use to be defined
